explanation: Uniform initialization is a practical C++ technique introduced in C++11 that uses curly braces {} to initialize variables, objects, and containers. It promotes best practices by providing a consistent and safe way to handle initialization across different types, preventing narrowing conversions (e.g., assigning a double to an int without explicit intent) and reducing errors in complex code. In real-world programming, this pattern is essential for writing idiomatic C++ code, as it works seamlessly with standard library containers, classes, and aggregates. Common pitfalls include mistakenly using parentheses for initialization, which can lead to unexpected conversions or ambiguities; to avoid this, always prefer braces for clarity and safety. This technique is widely used in scenarios like initializing data structures in game development, financial software, or any application dealing with collections and objects.
keywords: brace initialization, C++ uniform initialization, initializer list initialization, narrowing conversion
